dedupe_keys.name: resilience to climate change in the telecoms sector ofcom adaptation report 2024

description: This adaptation-planning case is the UK communications regulator's report, submitted to the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs on 19 December 2024, on how climate risks affect electronic communications networks and how the sector is adapting; it feeds the UK's fourth Climate Change Risk Assessment. It draws on the Climate Change Committee's finding that telecom infrastructure is at risk from all types of flooding, high winds and lightning, and that dependence on electricity supply is a reciprocal risk, and describes adaptation such as the permanent flood defences at vulnerable sites that the sector finished installing in 2018, Ofcom's revised security and resilience guidance with specific flood and climate requirements, and work with other regulators, government and industry. Earlier rounds were covered by reports from the trade body techUK on the core digital infrastructure (2016) and on network resilience. Coverage: the United Kingdom's fixed and mobile networks, to 2024 with forward-looking risks. Format and access: free PDF report and web page on Ofcom's site. Caveats: a regulator's summary based on industry information, without site-level risk data; the Ofcom website blocks some automated access. Simulation uses: climate adaptation planning of telecom networks, hazard exposure screening for flood and wind, and energy-telecom dependencies in cascading-failure models. Related records: the techUK data-centre adaptation report covers data centres, and ENISA incident reports give failure causes.
